target_customer: Fire protection, HVAC and security technicians and facilities teams who must locate devices inside buildings
problem: Field technicians waste time finding devices scattered in large buildings, and there are no cheap indoor maps or navigation without installing beacons.

founders.name: Will Huang
education: UC Berkeley, EECS M.Eng. program student (2018)
founders.background_notes: Berkeley EECS news names him as a 2018 U.S. Imagine Cup winner with the Pengram team.

founders.name: Bill Zhou
education: UC Berkeley graduate student (2018, surname Zhou per Berkeley and Microsoft coverage)
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; coverage of the Imagine Cup team names Zhou, Vedant Saran and Will Huang.

exit.reason: Cause not public. YC lists the company as inactive; no announcement or acquisition found.

competitors.name: Pointr
competitors.what: Indoor positioning and navigation platform for retail, transport and industrial sites (London)
competitors.traction_then: Series A round in progress in 2018
competitors.funding_then: Series A led by Livingbridge (amount unknown)

competitors.name: Navisens
competitors.what: Inertial smartphone tracking for indoor location and AR

technical_complexity.rationale: Mapping and localizing inside buildings from a phone camera and sensors with AR waypoints was hard for a two person student team in 2018, as inertial and visual positioning is research heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Indoor positioning vendors and phone AR toolkits could offer similar mapping; the technician niche gave focus but little lock-in.

market_need_then: Not independently sourced; the YC description frames technicians locating devices in buildings as the pain point.

branding.domain_note: Used pengramar.com, not an exact .com; no source on how it was obtained.
branding.community_and_virality: Won first place and the Mixed Reality Award at the 2018 U.S. Imagine Cup finals and a mixed reality award at the July 2018 world finals, per Berkeley and Microsoft coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: Only press is Imagine Cup award coverage as a student team; name is unusual but easy to misspell.

pivots.from: AR platform to holographically teleport remote engineers into a workspace (Imagine Cup project)
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the Imagine Cup description versus the YC description

outcome_analysis: Pengram grew out of a Berkeley student project that won the 2018 U.S. Imagine Cup and a mixed reality award, then joined YC in Winter 2019 as a two person team building phone-based indoor AR navigation for building technicians. Databases show only about 150 thousand dollars raised, no press after 2018, and the website is dead. No source explains why it stopped, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: pengramar.com returned HTTP 404, so the site is treated as dead. The 150K seed rests on database profiles (CB Insights and Village.ai); Crunchbase calls it pre-seed and no date is given. Location conflicts: YC says San Francisco, CB Insights Berkeley, VCBacked Santa Clara. The pivot is inferred from differing descriptions and is not stated by a source. The Pointr and Navisens source pages were seen as search results, not opened; Navisens is dated 2016, well before the batch, and Pointr 2018-08. Zhou's first name Bill comes from the YC page only.
